dbus_enabled.description: Enable or disable DBus inter-process communication.

debug_classes.description: Comma-separated list of classes to debug.

debug_methods.description: Comma-separated list of methods to debug.

default_profile.description: Name of the profile to use by default.

keybindings.description: Map of keybinding names to combinations. Example: {'split_h': 'Ctrl+Shift+O', 'new_tab': 'Ctrl+Shift+T'}.

layouts.description: Map of layout names to layout content strings.

profiles.description: List of terminal profile configurations. Each item defines appearance and behavior settings for a profile.

profiles_items.description:
Schema for individual profile items in the profiles list. Note: In this template, profiles are mapped by name in the values, but the schema here describes the structure if a flat list were used. However, per instructions for list-of-objects, we define items. But Terminator config maps profiles by name under [profiles]. To adhere to the Jinja2 constraint `for name, profile in profiles.items()`, `profiles` should be a map-like structure in the values, but the schema type must be string|number|bool|list. A map is not a supported type. I will use a list of objects and render them using a key-based approach if possible, or simplify to a list. Given the template uses `items()`, I will assume the `profiles` value is a list of objects, and I will change the template to iterate over the list and assign keys, OR I will use a list and iterate. The prompt says `for x in list`. It doesn't explicitly forbid iterating over a list of dicts. I will use a list of dicts and iterate. To allow naming the section, I'll include a `name` field in the item. The Jinja2 loop `for name, profile` requires a dict. If I provide a list, I must use `for profile in profiles`. I will update the template to use `for profile in profiles` and access `profile.name`. This is safer for the `type: list` constraint. Re-writing template logic mentally: `[profiles]
{% for profile in profiles %}
[{{ profile.name }}]
...
{% endfor %}`. This is cleaner. I will adjust the template accordingly.
